title: Online end-session that fails on the network loses mood/notes and resurrects the workout
description: In submitEndSession the online branch fires endExercise(...) for each open exercise and then endWorkout(session.id, {end_time, notes, feedback: mood}). If the network drops during this sequence (endExercise calls succeed but endWorkout throws, or endWorkout itself throws), the catch at line 345 detects isNetworkFailure and calls persistInProgressSession(state). That helper (offline.ts:97) writes status:'in_progress' and NEVER captures end_mood/end_notes/endedAt — unlike the offline branch at lines 291-301 which writes status:'pending_sync' with end_mood. So the end intent is dropped. On reconnect syncOne (offline.ts:163) sees status==='in_progress', skips the endWorkout block at line 269, and because session.id>0 deletes the record at line 283 after only re-ending exercises. The workout end_time/feedback is never set on the server, so workoutIsActive() (backend.ts:14, end_time<=start_time) still reports it active and the next refreshFromBackend (backend.ts:24-42) restores it as the current in-progress session — the ended workout silently reappears and the mood/notes are gone.
attackOrTrigger: Route '/', user online mid-workout taps End with a mood selected; connectivity drops during the end request. If the user reloads or navigates away instead of manually re-tapping End, mood + end notes are lost and on reconnect the workout re-opens as active.
why: A completed workout silently loses its feedback/notes and comes back to life as in-progress; the user believes the session was saved and ended.
fixSketch: In the network-failure catch of submitEndSession, persist a pending_sync record carrying end_mood/end_notes/endedAt (reuse the offline-branch save at lines 291-301) instead of the plain persistInProgressSession, so syncOne runs the endWorkout replay on reconnect.

verdicts.title: Online end-session that fails on the network loses mood/notes and resurrects the workout
verdicts.reason: Confirmed against session.ts:268-355 and offline.ts:89-110. The online branch never captures mood/end_notes into a local 'ended' object (that object is only built in the offline branch at line 281) — it just calls endExercise/endWorkout on the raw session. On a network failure in that block, state.currentSession is still the untouched pre-end session (it's only nulled at line 338, after endWorkout succeeds), so the catch's persistInProgressSession(state) at offline.ts:89-110 reads that unmodified session and writes status:'in_progress' with no end_mood/end_notes/endedAt, exactly as claimed. In syncOne (verified in sync.ts, formerly offline.ts logic now inlined at actions/sync.ts... actually offline.ts:163-ish / actions/sync.ts syncOne), the pending_sync+end_mood branch is gated on status==='pending_sync', so an 'in_progress' record skips the endWorkout call and, since session.id>0, the record is deleted after only re-ending exercises — matching the claimed drop of the end intent.

verdicts.title: Online end-session that fails on the network loses mood/notes and resurrects the workout
verdicts.reason: Reachability holds. Verified in session.ts:308-355: the online branch runs endExercise for each open exercise via Promise.all, then calls endWorkout separately at line 330. A network drop specifically during/after the endExercise calls but during the endWorkout call is a plausible flaky-connectivity scenario (not a contrived race) — it doesn't require simultaneous failure, just a drop that outlasts the first batch of requests but hits the second. Critically, state.currentSession is only cleared at line 338, which sits AFTER the endWorkout call; if endWorkout throws, execution jumps straight to the catch block with currentSession still populated and unmodified (mood/notes never written into the session object, only passed as separate args to the failed endWorkout call). The catch's isNetworkFailure branch then persists that stale in-progress session via persistInProgressSession with no path to attach end_mood/end_notes, matching the claim. A user tapping 'End' while online on a real mobile connection with degrading signal is an ordinary, reachable trigger, and there is no client guard that would intercept this sequence before it reaches the network calls.

verdicts.title: Online end-session that fails on the network loses mood/notes and resurrects the workout
verdicts.reason: Read session.ts:260-356 directly. The catch block at line 346-349 for the online end-session path calls only the generic persistInProgressSession(state) helper on network failure -- the same helper used for other in-progress-session network failures elsewhere in the file (lines 170, 250) -- with no capture of mood, endNotes, or endedAt. This is asymmetric with the offline branch (lines 289-301), which explicitly persists end_mood/end_notes under status:'pending_sync'. There is no sanitizer, guard, debounce-flush, or idempotency key in this file that recovers the end-intent in the online-failure path; the claim is not already mitigated.

title: A single unparseable/old-shape offline record aborts syncing of ALL pending sessions
description: syncPendingSessions loops over every offline record sequentially with await syncOne(record, ...) and no per-record try/catch. syncOne dereferences the stored session shape directly (offline.ts:207 ex.settings.length, 231 ex.sets.map, 253 ex.settings.map) and OfflineSessionRecord (todaySessions.ts:7) has NO version field and no validation/migration on read (kvGet in storage.ts:56 returns the raw JSON cast to the type). If any record was written by an older client whose exercise shape lacked settings or sets (or is partially corrupt), syncOne throws a TypeError. That is not a network failure, so the catch at sync.ts:69 sets state.error and the loop aborts — every OTHER pending session at/after the poison record never syncs. Because records are listed newest-first (todaySessions.ts:47) and the poison one is not removed, the block is permanent across reconnects.
attackOrTrigger: User upgrades the PWA across a release that changed the persisted session shape while an offline session sits pending; on reconnect the first record throws and no offline workout ever reaches the server.
why: One corrupt/version-skewed record indefinitely strands every queued offline workout as unsynced with no recovery path.
fixSketch: Wrap each syncOne call in its own try/catch so a bad record is skipped/quarantined without blocking the rest, and add a version field to OfflineSessionRecord plus a validating/migrating read that drops or upgrades unknown shapes.

verdicts.title: A single unparseable/old-shape offline record aborts syncing of ALL pending sessions
verdicts.reason: Confirmed in sync.ts:40-79 and offline.ts's syncOne: the for-loop at sync.ts:54 has no per-iteration try/catch, only one try wrapping the entire loop. syncOne unconditionally dereferences ex.settings.length, ex.sets.map, and ex.settings.map without any shape validation. A throw from a malformed record lands in the outer catch (sync.ts:69), and since it isn't a network error, state.error is set and the loop exits — any records after the poison one in the array are never attempted. The mechanism is real as written in the cited files.

title: Read-modify-write race in persistInProgressSession drops merge-only fields (deletions / id map)
description: persistInProgressSession does a load-then-save: const existing = await loadOfflineSession(key) (line 96) then builds a record preserving existing.server_exercise_ids_by_local / deleted_server_exercise_ids / cancel_workout (lines 102-105) and saves. The await on load yields the event loop, so two overlapping persists interleave and the later save clobbers the earlier one's merge-only fields. removeExercise (core.ts:256-262) reads existing.deleted_server_exercise_ids and calls persistInProgressSession with extra {deleted_server_exercise_ids:[...,exId]}. If a plain persist (e.g. the unawaited void persistInProgressSession(state) in the offline handler, sync.ts:91, or an in-flight set action's persist) loaded existing before removeExercise's save landed, it writes back the old deleted list and the deletion is lost. On reconnect syncOne never calls cancelExercise for that id, so a deleted server exercise persists (or a lost server_exercise_ids_by_local entry makes createExercise run twice → duplicate exercise).
attackOrTrigger: Offline / connectivity dropping: user removes a previously-synced exercise while another persist is in flight — e.g. the window 'offline' handler's fire-and-forget persist overlaps the removeExercise persist. Last write wins on the whole record and the merge field is silently reverted.
why: A user's offline deletion of an exercise (or the create-idempotency map) is silently lost, leaving deleted data on the server or duplicating exercises on reconnect.
fixSketch: Serialize offline writes through a single-flight queue (or do the read-modify-write inside one IndexedDB transaction / a merge function) so concurrent persists cannot clobber each other's merge-only fields; at minimum await, never fire-and-forget, the offline-event persist.

verdicts.title: Read-modify-write race in persistInProgressSession drops merge-only fields (deletions / id map)
verdicts.reason: Confirmed in offline.ts:89-110: persistInProgressSession does `await loadOfflineSession(key)` then builds and saves a new record merging in existing.server_exercise_ids_by_local / deleted_server_exercise_ids / cancel_workout plus any `extra`. The await is a genuine yield point, so two concurrent invocations (e.g. the unawaited `void persistInProgressSession(state)` fired from the 'offline' handler at sync.ts:91) can interleave load/save and the later save can overwrite the earlier one's extra fields with stale existing-data. Nothing in the cited code serializes or version-checks these writes, so the described last-write-wins race is real as written.

title: No quota/IndexedDB error handling — a failed persist silently discards the just-logged set
description: kvSet awaits store.put with no handling for QuotaExceededError or a rejected/aborted IndexedDB transaction (the localStorage fallback at line 64 also throws on quota). The offline write path updates in-memory state FIRST and persists AFTER: addSet offline (sets.ts:170-190) sets currentSession then await persistInProgressSession(state) -> saveOfflineSession -> kvSet. If that put rejects (storage pressure / eviction / quota), the rejection propagates to the action's catch, which is only guarded for isNetworkFailure — a QuotaExceededError lands in the generic branch (sets.ts:230 state.error.set) while the set is already shown in the UI but was never durably written. On reload/crash the set is gone. persistentStorage.ts only requests persistence (best-effort, often denied on non-installed iOS Safari) and nothing verifies it or reacts to a failed write.
attackOrTrigger: Offline session on a device under storage pressure or an origin without granted persistent storage; a set/exercise is added, the IndexedDB put fails, the user sees the entry on screen, then reloads — the entry is silently absent.
why: Logged workout data appears saved in the UI but is never persisted and is lost on the next reload, with only a generic error surfaced.
fixSketch: Detect write failures in kvSet (catch QuotaExceededError / transaction abort) and surface a distinct 'could not save locally' state so the UI does not present unpersisted edits as saved; consider verifying navigator.storage.persisted() and warning when best-effort storage is in use.

verdicts.title: No quota/IndexedDB error handling — a failed persist silently discards the just-logged set
verdicts.reason: Confirmed in storage.ts:60-69: kvSet's IndexedDB path is `await withStore('readwrite', (store) => store.put(...))` with no try/catch around it, and the localStorage fallback path (line 64) calls `localStorage.setItem` directly, which throws synchronously on quota exceeded — neither path swallows or handles a quota/abort error. Any rejection would propagate up to the caller unhandled at this layer, matching the claim that storage.ts itself has zero quota/error handling.

title: scopedKey falls back to an unscoped key when the active user id is unknown, orphaning offline sessions
description: scopedKey returns the bare base key when getActiveUserId() is null (localStorage 'auth.activeUserId' unset or unreadable). All offline session keys (todaySessions.ts:22-28), the recent-sessions cache (offline.ts:18) and planned-template keys route through scopedKey. If any persist happens while activeUserId is null (value not yet written after session restore, or localStorage throwing in the try/catch at scope.ts:9-14), the record is stored under the unscoped base key; once the user id is later populated, every read uses the 'u<id>:' prefix and never finds that record, so an in-progress offline session written in the null window is orphaned and lost. The same unscoped record is also visible to a different user on the same device during their own null window (listOfflineSessions with an empty scope prefix enumerates it), a weak cross-user data-leak surface.
attackOrTrigger: App writes an offline session during a window where auth.activeUserId is not yet set (cold start / restore race, or localStorage access throwing); after the id resolves, the scoped read misses the base-keyed record and the session is silently gone.
why: An in-progress offline workout can be orphaned (lost) across the auth-resolution boundary, and an unscoped record is momentarily readable by another account on a shared device.
fixSketch: Refuse to persist (or defer) offline session writes until a concrete user id is known, or key such writes under an explicit 'anonymous' namespace migrated to the real user id on login rather than silently sharing the unscoped base key.
